newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek short rates to near 11.9pct on fx outflows.
newsitem.headline: Greek short rates to near 11.9pct on fx outflows.

text.p: Short-term drachma rates will approach 11.90 percent if forex outflows continue but the recent fluctuations in ecu/drachma do not signal a change in Greece's foreign exchange policy, a central bank official told Reuters.

"Short-term interest rates will hover in the 9.90-11.90 percent range depending on prevailing liquidity conditions," the central bank official said. "If forex outflows continue, short-term rates will approach the 11.90 percent level."
The central bank set up a two-tier deposit facility acccepting up to 300 billion drachmas from banks at the basic rate of 11.90 percent and any amount at the floor rate of 9.90 percent.
The interbank liquidity surplus amounted to over 700 billion drachmas, sharply down from 1.5 trillion drachmas when Bank of Greece introduced its deposit facility in March.
Bank of Greece drained 400 billion drachmas of 14-day funds in its regular weekly depo tenders, 300 billion drachmas at the basic rate of 11.90 percent and a small sum at 9.90 percent, he said.

"The short-term fluctuations of the drachma against the ecu do not reflect any changes in the pre-announced foreign exchange policy," the official said. "The direction of the monetary and foreign exchange policy has not changed."
The central bank has said that the foreign exchange policy will remain anti-inflationary in 1997 and wants the drachma to be broadly stable against the currencies that make up the ecu.
The Bank of Greece has sold more than 1.2 billion ecus for drachmas at the fixing this week to support the drachma and keep the ecu/drachma cross in check.
Ecu/drachma settled at 312 at the fixing on Thursday, slightly up from 311.90 on Wednesday.
